ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-1: Zero-price bypass in validateHandlerOrder — computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, validateHandlerOrder does not check for zero (unlike _validatePricingBounds)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on uint160 overflow. In validateHandlerOrder: if minSqrtPriceX96 != 0, then 0 < min reverts. If only max bound set, 0 > max is false so it passes. But validateHandlerOrder is VIEW-ONLY — no state modification, no extraction path. Pool swap pricing uses pool type's getCurrentPriceX96, not computeRatioX96. CLOB amounts are bounded by uint128 max, preventing overflow in practice.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-2: Direct handler call bypassing pricing enforcement — calling CLOBTransferHandler.ammHandleTransfer directly
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ammHandleTransfer has explicit caller check: msg.sender != AMM reverts. afterSwapRefund also AMM-gated. All state-changing handler functions require AMM caller. openOrder/closeOrder are separate user-facing functions that don't settle swaps.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-3: Settings sync gap — setTokenSettings may leave stale memSettings in CreatorHookSettingsRegistry
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Registry stores memSettings with initialized=true but passes original settings (possibly initialized=false) to hooks. Self-heals: _getOrFetchTokenSettings re-fetches from registry when !initialized. Impact is one extra external call (gas waste), not security issue.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: KV-4: Transient storage leak — DIRECT_SWAP_BEFORE_SWAP_AMOUNT_SLOT not cleared on all paths
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Transient storage auto-clears per-tx. Within same directSwap: both tokens' beforeSwap hooks write same swapAmount. Direct swap uses DIRECT_SWAP_GUARD_FLAG preventing re-entry. Known as HOOK-001. Cross-contract tstore is impossible by EVM design (EIP-1153 is contract-scoped).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C1: Pool type lies about amountOut — Core credits user more than reserves hold
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Core uses _safeDecrementUint128(reserve, amountOut) which reverts on underflow. Double protection: reserve accounting + actual ERC20 transfer (SafeERC20.safeTransfer would fail if balance insufficient).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C2: Handler receives mismatched token pair from Core
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Handler trusts AMM caller. AMM validates tokens match pool in _poolSwapByInput before calling handler. Handler requires msg.sender == AMM. Mismatch would require bug in AMMModule itself, not a boundary issue.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C3: Hook returns manipulated fee > swap amount
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _applySwapByInputInputFees checks feeAmount > swapAmountIn and reverts at AMMModule L2616/L2629. Output fees also bounded at L2711/L2723.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C4: Settings change between beforeSwap and afterSwap via reentrancy or multi-call
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Reentrancy guard (ENTERED flag) prevents any re-entry during swap. Settings cached in memory during execution. Even if registry updates between hooks, fees are independent per hook call — no cross-reference between beforeSwap and afterSwap fee values.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C5: Pool type returns feeAmount > amountIn
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _validateProtocolFees at AMMModule:1654-1677 explicitly checks totalFees > amountIn and reverts with LBAMM__FeeAmountExceedsInputAmount.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C6: Handler→External reentrancy via MaliciousToken callback
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Reentrancy guard (ENTERED bit in TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags) is active during all external calls including token transfers. _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) at AMMModule:3190 preserves ENTERED bit — only clears custom flags. MaliciousToken callback hitting any AMM entry point would hit the reentrancy guard.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C7/INV-H01: Hook callback access control — calling hook functions from external address
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All state-changing hook functions (beforeSwap, afterSwap, validateAddLiquidity, validatePoolCreation) enforce _requireCallerIsAMM(). validateRemoveLiquidity always reverts (not supported). validateHandlerOrder is view-only — no extraction path even without access control.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C8/INV-H02: Settlement conservation — handler sends less/more than expected
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Strict equality balance check at AMMModule:2208: balanceInBefore + amountIn != balanceInAfter reverts. Even 1 wei difference is caught. Protects against fee-on-transfer tokens and handler misbehavior.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C9/INV-H04: Hook fee overflow in _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Hook fees are bounded by swap amount — each hook fee subtracted from adjustedAmountSpecified. Additionally, tokensOwed is decremented before transfer (CEI pattern). Reentrancy guard (ENTERED bit) preserved during fee execution. executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers requires msg.sender == address(this) at ModuleFeeCollection:128.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C10/INV-SW04: Swap output exceeds pre-swap reserves
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _safeDecrementUint128(reserveOut, amountOut) reverts on underflow. Pool type cannot output more than reserves.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C11/INV-S04: Denomination consistency — fee computation vs transfer token mismatch
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Traced fee flow through all paths: (1) Swap fees always in tokenIn, computed and applied before pool swap. (2) Hook fees stored via _storeHookFees with (tokenFor, tokenFee) key — denomination preserved in key and used correctly in _transferHookFeesByHook. (3) Flash loan: _storeHookFees(loanToken, feeToken, ...) uses separate key, feeAmount -= tokenFeeAmount is safe because feeAmount = tokenFeeAmount + protocolPortion. (4) Flash loan _collectToken has strict balance check.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: _storeHookFees key includes both tokenFor and tokenFee; _transferHookFeesByHook transfers tokenFee

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C12/INV-E03: Sandwich attack — victim doesn't receive limitAmount
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: AMMModule:2156 enforces amountOut >= swapOrder.limitAmount. If sandwich moves price, victim's swap reverts if output falls below their limit. This is the standard slippage protection.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C13: PoolDecoder with max/edge values
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: PoolDecoder.getPoolType does shr(144, poolId) extracting top 112 bits. With max poolId, returns address with 6 leading zero bytes (by construction). Pool type addresses must have 6 leading zero bytes — max value is 2^112-1. createPool validates pool type address has code.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C14: createPool with edge parameters (zero tick spacing, max fee, etc.)
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool creation delegates to pool type's createPool, which validates parameters internally. Core validates pool type has code and 6 leading zero bytes. Edge parameters would be rejected by pool type's own validation (e.g., tick spacing must be > 0 for Dynamic pools).
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: pool type validates own parameters

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C15: Storage slot collision across diamond facets
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All modules use shared AppStorage at deterministic slot 0x9A1D via Storage.appStorage(). No conventional storage variables (Slither shows 0 storage slots for AMMModule and ModuleAdmin). Pool types are external contracts with msg.sender-keyed storage, not diamond facets. TstorishReentrancyGuardWithFlags uses separate transient storage slot.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Forged hook caller — call hook with fake pool identity
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: msg.sender cannot be forged in EVM. Hook's AMM address is immutable (set at construction). All state-changing hooks check _requireCallerIsAMM().

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Cross-contract transient-slot theft
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: EIP-1153 transient storage is contract-scoped. Contract A cannot read/write Contract B's transient storage. The only within-contract issue is HOOK-001 (beforeSwap overwrite for second token).

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Reentrancy during hook fee distribution — _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) clears guard
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: _setReentrancyFlags(NO_FLAGS) clears custom flags but preserves ENTERED bit (L68-72: flags & ~(ENTERED|NOT_ENTERED) = 0; currentGuard = tstorish & ENTERED preserves ENTERED; result = ENTERED | 0 = ENTERED). Reentrancy guard remains active during _executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Dust-loop extraction — 100+ tiny swaps drain pool via rounding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Fee calculations use FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp (rounds UP in protocol's favor). Pool type swap math rounds against user. Each tiny swap loses dust to protocol, not attacker.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: FullMath.mulDivRoundingUp rounds up for fees

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Permit mutation — replay with mutated feeOnTop
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: feeOnTop intentionally unsigned (known design). limitAmount IS signed, caps total signer exposure. recipient IS signed. Only feeOnTop can be mutated but limitAmount prevents overspending.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Diamond storage-slot collision — deploy facet writing to another's slot
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Single deterministic storage slot 0x9A1D for all AMM state. Pool types are external (not delegatecall). Adding facets requires admin access.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: LBAMMStorage.sol fixed slot, pool types external

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Flash loan denomination mismatch — feeToken != loanToken causes accounting error
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: When feeToken != loanToken: (1) loan repayment checked via separate balance check for loanToken, (2) fee collection checked via separate balance check for feeToken, (3) _storeHookFees key includes both loanToken and feeToken preserving denomination, (4) feeAmount -= tokenFeeAmount is safe since feeAmount = tokenFeeAmount + protocolPortion (always >= tokenFeeAmount), (5) _storeProtocolFees uses feeToken consistently.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: AMMModule.sol L3288-3382, _storeHookFees key preserves denomination

ruled_out_vectors.vector: Pool type addLiquidity return value mismatch — LP gets free shares
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type returns (deposit0, deposit1, fees0, fees1). Core updates reserves with _safeIncrementUint128 using these values, then collects tokens via _distributeAndCollectLiquidityTokens which uses _collectToken with strict balance check (balanceAfter == balanceBefore + amount). Pool type manages its own position state — inconsistent return values would corrupt its own tracking. User has min/max bounds (L429-435).
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: AMMModule.sol L397-488, _collectToken strict balance check at L2917

ruled_out_vectors.vector: executeQueuedHookFeesByHookTransfers callable externally
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: ModuleFeeCollection:127-133 requires msg.sender == address(this). External callers cannot invoke this function. Only called as a self-call from AMMModule swap/liquidity finalization paths.
ruled_out_vectors.test_file: N/A — code evidence: ModuleFeeCollection.sol L128: msg.sender != address(this) reverts

theft_theses.thesis: Pool type can lie about swap output, crediting user more than reserves hold
Direct call to handler bypasses hook pricing enforcement, enabling unfair fills
Transient storage leak between direct swaps enables price manipulation
Hook fee manipulation extracts value from swap users
Reentrancy during hook fee distribution enables re-entry into swap
Flash loan denomination mismatch when feeToken != loanToken enables accounting error
Pool type addLiquidity returns inflated values, LP gets free shares without depositing
